title: An RPN calculator
description:
Build a calculator for **Reverse Polish Notation**, where the operator comes after its numbers: `3 4 +` is 7, and `3 4 + 2 *` is (3 + 4) × 2. No brackets are needed, and it is exactly how a stack works: numbers are pushed, and an operator pops two, works them out, and pushes the answer. Old HP calculators and the Forth and PostScript languages work this way, and so does the Java virtual machine.

Read lines until the input ends. Each line is one calculation of tokens separated by spaces; print its result, or an error:

```
3 4 +
3 4 + 2 *
10 3 -
-7 2 /
-7 2 %
2 3 4 * +
5 0 /
1 +
1 2
4 x
```

prints

```
7
14
7
-3
-1
14
error: division by zero
error: not enough numbers
error: 2 numbers left
error: unknown token x
```

| Token | Does |
|---|---|
| a whole number, perhaps with a `-` in front | pushes it |
| `+ - * /` | pops b, then a, and pushes a + b, a − b, a × b, a ÷ b (rounded towards zero) |
| `%` | the remainder, with the sign of a, as in C |
| `dup` | pushes a copy of the top number |
| `swap` | swaps the top two |

- A line ends with exactly one number on the stack: print it. More than one: `error: N numbers left`. None (an empty line): print nothing.
- An operator with fewer than two numbers (one for `dup`): `error: not enough numbers`. Dividing by zero: `error: division by zero`. Anything else: `error: unknown token ` and the token. After an error, skip the rest of the line.
- A lone `-` is subtraction; `-` followed by digits is a negative number.
- At most 100 numbers on the stack, and lines of at most 200 characters.

        section .text

solution.main.asm:
global  _start

MAX     equ     100
TOKEN_NUMBER  equ 1
TOKEN_UNKNOWN equ 0

        section .bss
line:   resb    256
stack:  resq    MAX
depth:  resq    1

        section .data
s_div0:   db    "error: division by zero", 10, 0
s_short:  db    "error: not enough numbers", 10, 0
s_left1:  db    "error: ", 0
s_left2:  db    " numbers left", 10, 0
s_unknown: db   "error: unknown token ", 0
s_full:   db    "error: too many numbers", 10, 0
w_dup:    db    "dup", 0
w_swap:   db    "swap", 0

        section .text
; push_num: rdi = a value. Returns rax = 1, or 0 if the stack is full.
push_num:
        mov     rax, [rel depth]
        cmp     rax, MAX
        jae     .full
        lea     rcx, [rel stack]
        mov     [rcx + rax*8], rdi
        inc     qword [rel depth]
        mov     eax, 1
        ret
.full:  xor     eax, eax
        ret

; pop_num: returns rax = the value (only call it when depth > 0).
pop_num:
        dec     qword [rel depth]
        mov     rax, [rel depth]
        lea     rcx, [rel stack]
        mov     rax, [rcx + rax*8]
        ret

; same_word: rdi = token start, rsi = its length, rdx = a zero-terminated word. Returns 1 if equal.
same_word:
        xor     ecx, ecx
.loop:  cmp     rcx, rsi
        je      .end
        movzx   eax, byte [rdx + rcx]
        cmp     al, [rdi + rcx]
        jne     .no
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .loop
.end:   cmp     byte [rdx + rcx], 0
        jne     .no
        mov     eax, 1
        ret
.no:    xor     eax, eax
        ret

; parse_number: rdi = token start, rsi = its length.
; Returns rax = TOKEN_NUMBER with the value in rdx, or TOKEN_UNKNOWN.
parse_number:
        xor     r8d, r8d                ; 1 if negative
        xor     edx, edx                ; the value
        xor     ecx, ecx                ; position
        cmp     byte [rdi], '-'
        jne     .digits
        mov     r8d, 1
        inc     rcx
        cmp     rcx, rsi
        je      .no                     ; a lone '-' is not a number
.digits:
        cmp     rcx, rsi
        je      .done
        movzx   eax, byte [rdi + rcx]
        sub     eax, '0'
        cmp     eax, 9
        ja      .no
        imul    rdx, rdx, 10
        add     rdx, rax
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .digits
.done:  test    r8d, r8d
        jz      .yes
        neg     rdx
.yes:   mov     eax, TOKEN_NUMBER
        ret
.no:    mov     eax, TOKEN_UNKNOWN
        ret

; binary_op: dil = the operator character. Pops b and a, pushes the result.
; Returns 0 when it worked, 1 for not enough numbers, 2 for division by zero.
binary_op:
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        push    r13
        mov     ebx, edi
        cmp     qword [rel depth], 2
        jb      .short
        call    pop_num
        mov     r13, rax                ; b
        call    pop_num
        mov     r12, rax                ; a
        cmp     bl, '+'
        jne     .not_add
        lea     rdi, [r12 + r13]
        jmp     .push
.not_add:
        cmp     bl, '-'
        jne     .not_sub
        mov     rdi, r12
        sub     rdi, r13
        jmp     .push
.not_sub:
        cmp     bl, '*'
        jne     .divide
        mov     rdi, r12
        imul    rdi, r13
        jmp     .push
.divide:
        test    r13, r13
        jz      .zero
        mov     rax, r12
        cqo
        idiv    r13
        mov     rdi, rax                ; the quotient
        cmp     bl, '%'
        jne     .push
        mov     rdi, rdx                ; the remainder
.push:  call    push_num
        xor     eax, eax
        jmp     .out
.short: mov     eax, 1
        jmp     .out
.zero:  mov     eax, 2
.out:   pop     r13
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

; run_line: rdi = a zero-terminated line. Works it out and prints the result or an error.
run_line:
        push    rbx                     ; the current position
        push    r12                     ; the token's start
        push    r13                     ; the token's length
        mov     rbx, rdi
        mov     qword [rel depth], 0
.token:
        cmp     byte [rbx], ' '
        jne     .start
        inc     rbx
        jmp     .token
.start: cmp     byte [rbx], 0
        je      .end_of_line
        mov     r12, rbx
.scan:  movzx   eax, byte [rbx]
        test    al, al
        jz      .scanned
        cmp     al, ' '
        je      .scanned
        inc     rbx
        jmp     .scan
.scanned:
        mov     r13, rbx
        sub     r13, r12

        cmp     r13, 1                  ; a one-character operator?
        jne     .words
        movzx   edi, byte [r12]
        cmp     dil, '+'
        je      .operator
        cmp     dil, '-'
        je      .operator
        cmp     dil, '*'
        je      .operator
        cmp     dil, '/'
        je      .operator
        cmp     dil, '%'
        je      .operator
        jmp     .words
.operator:
        call    binary_op
        cmp     eax, 1
        je      .err_short
        cmp     eax, 2
        je      .err_zero
        jmp     .token

.words:
        mov     rdi, r12
        mov     rsi, r13
        lea     rdx, [rel w_dup]
        call    same_word
        test    eax, eax
        jz      .not_dup
        cmp     qword [rel depth], 1
        jb      .err_short
        mov     rax, [rel depth]
        lea     rcx, [rel stack]
        mov     rdi, [rcx + rax*8 - 8]
        call    push_num
        test    eax, eax
        jz      .err_full
        jmp     .token
.not_dup:
        mov     rdi, r12
        mov     rsi, r13
        lea     rdx, [rel w_swap]
        call    same_word
        test    eax, eax
        jz      .number
        cmp     qword [rel depth], 2
        jb      .err_short
        mov     rax, [rel depth]
        lea     rcx, [rel stack]
        mov     rdx, [rcx + rax*8 - 8]
        mov     rsi, [rcx + rax*8 - 16]
        mov     [rcx + rax*8 - 8], rsi
        mov     [rcx + rax*8 - 16], rdx
        jmp     .token
.number:
        mov     rdi, r12
        mov     rsi, r13
        call    parse_number
        cmp     eax, TOKEN_NUMBER
        jne     .err_unknown
        mov     rdi, rdx
        call    push_num
        test    eax, eax
        jz      .err_full
        jmp     .token

.end_of_line:
        mov     rax, [rel depth]
        test    rax, rax
        jz      .done                   ; an empty line: nothing to print
        cmp     rax, 1
        jne     .err_left
        call    pop_num
        mov     rdi, rax
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline
        jmp     .done
.err_left:
        lea     rdi, [rel s_left1]
        call    print_str
        mov     rdi, [rel depth]
        call    print_int
        lea     rdi, [rel s_left2]
        call    print_str
        jmp     .done
.err_short:
        lea     rdi, [rel s_short]
        call    print_str
        jmp     .done
.err_zero:
        lea     rdi, [rel s_div0]
        call    print_str
        jmp     .done
.err_full:
        lea     rdi, [rel s_full]
        call    print_str
        jmp     .done
.err_unknown:
        lea     rdi, [rel s_unknown]
        call    print_str
        mov     byte [r12 + r13], 0     ; end the token there, to print it
        mov     rdi, r12
        call    print_str
        call    print_newline
.done:  pop     r13
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

_start:
.next:
        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        mov     esi, 256
        call    read_line
        cmp     rax, -1
        je      .exit
        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        call    run_line
        jmp     .next
.exit:
        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

requirements: Keep the calculator's stack in an array in `.bss` with its own count, not on the machine stack.
Write a function that parses one token: a number (with its value), an operator, or something unknown.
Use `idiv` with `cqo` for `/` and `%`, and print with `print_int`.
